name: Argument Density Score
description: Measures the ratio of distinct, non-redundant claims and premises extracted from a text against its total physical word count.
mechanism: This method evaluates the informational efficiency of a text. When instructed to generate long texts, LLMs frequently engage in 'argumentative padding'—producing verbose paragraphs that eloquently circle around a single main point without introducing any novel claims, evidence, or nuance. They do this to meet length constraints without risking hallucination or breaking safety guardrails. By extracting the absolute number of distinct argumentative propositions (claims, premises, backing) and computing their ratio to the physical length of the text, this method yields an 'argument density score.' Exceptionally high word counts paired with a mathematically low number of distinct propositions strongly indicate the syntactic fluff typical of an AI attempting to hit a word count, whereas human experts instinctively write with much denser informational efficiency.
useCase: Detecting overly verbose AI-generated essays, op-eds, and reports that sound highly persuasive but lack the dense layering of actual substantive claims typical of human experts.
strengths:
• Directly targets the fundamental 'hallucination avoidance' padding behavior of LLMs.
• Exceptionally effective at analyzing long-form content, such as collegiate essays or automated journalism.
• Operates independently of specific vocabulary choices, meaning traditional 'rewrite' prompts cannot easily bypass it.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when evaluating human writers notoriously practicing 'word count padding' (e.g., struggling students).
• Completely ineffective on naturally sparse genres like poetry, minimalist fiction, or marketing slogans.
• Requires highly accurate propositional parsing logic to avoid counting rephrased identical claims as distinct.
parameters:
Analysis: Linguistic Proposition Extraction
Metric: Distinct Semantic Claims per 1000 Tokens
Output: 0-100 Informational Padding Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-84%. Highly accurate on essays, op-eds, and analytical pieces.

references.title: Stab, C. & Gurevych, I. (2017). Parsing Argumentation Structures in Persuasive Essays. Computational Linguistics.
